source.name: Adobe Inc. FY2025 Form 10-K (XBRL company facts, CIK 0000796343)
source.notes: Adobe does not tag annual recurring revenue in XBRL -- no issuer does; ARR is a management metric with no fixed definition. This case therefore uses disclosed FY2024 Revenues (21,505 $mm, period ending 2024-11-29) net of the services-mix driver as the opening SUBSCRIPTION ARR scale (20,878.6 $mm), so modelled total revenue stays on the same basis as disclosed revenue. It is a proxy and errs in a known direction: revenue is a flow averaged over a year while ARR is a point-in-time contracted balance, so for a growing business it understates exit ARR. The size of the error is measurable and is not hidden: modelled Year 1 revenue is 22,637 $mm against Adobe's disclosed FY2025 23,769 $mm, a gap of -4.76%. Ratios on this case are sourced; absolute dollar levels carry that gap.

source.name: Adobe Inc. FY2025 Form 10-K (XBRL company facts, CIK 0000796343)
source.notes: The four ARR flow rates are individually undisclosed. Their NET is pinned to Adobe's disclosed revenue growth of 0.1053 (FY2025 23,769 over FY2024 21,505 $mm), used as a proxy for net ARR growth. Gross churn is the balancing residual that carries this constraint, which is why it is the one flow rate with a real basis. Downside uses the lowest growth of the three most recent disclosed fiscal years (0.1024).

source.notes: Adobe's XBRL facts contain no ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense concept, so this line is the operating-expense residual: GrossProfit - OperatingIncomeLoss - SellingAndMarketingExpense - GeneralAndAdministrativeExpense. It is BROADER than Adobe's reported R&D line because it also absorbs amortization of intangibles and any other separately reported operating expense. Using the residual keeps modelled GAAP operating margin tied exactly to the disclosed 0.3663; a hand-picked R&D percentage would not.
